subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should third-party plugins be allowed to synchronously veto persisted config writes, and if so which writers and failure policy are in scope?
rationale: The missing interception seam is source-proven, but plugin authority over operator configuration, recovery paths, timeout behavior, and fail-open or fail-closed handling cannot be safely selected without maintainer intent.

options.title: Narrow control-plane veto
options.body: Add a bounded typed veto for gateway config.set, config.patch, and config.apply after canonical validation and SecretRef preflight but before persistence.

options.title: Core validation only
options.body: Keep veto authority in core and extend schemas, plugin-owned validation contracts, and agent mutation policy for newly identified unsafe changes.

options.title: Universal shared-write hook
options.body: Intercept gateway, CLI, install, doctor, and SDK mutation helpers through one contract, accepting much higher recursion and recovery-path complexity.

recommendation.title: Narrow control-plane veto
recommendation.body: Add a bounded typed veto for gateway config.set, config.patch, and config.apply after canonical validation and SecretRef preflight but before persistence.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main feature-history signal spans the central config-write, hook, SDK, and agent-guard surfaces involved in this decision.
